_doc: #564 THE ONE MAP from an app's REAL installer (PackageManager.getInstallSourceInfo().installingPackageName) to the Store ▸ Phone Apps origin button. Read by PhoneAppActions; nothing else in the store names an installer package. Foreign store -> the button opens that store's own page for the app ({pkg} is substituted, and the intent is aimed at the installer so market:// lands in the store that installed it, not whichever handler wins). `ours` is a Cloud fleet member (by the fleet manifest, or installed by this app) -> the host's Store ▸ Cloud page, where we update it. `unknown` is anything else (sideloaded APK, adb, no installer recorded) -> the system App info screen. Adding a store = one entry under `sources`.

resolver._doc: #571 WE ARE THE STORE. Per EXTERNAL app, the ORDERED install sources this store tries on a phone that has no other store: `vendor` = the vendor's own official direct-APK endpoint; `fdroid` = the official F-Droid repo (index-v1.jar, JAR-signed by the pinned `cert_sha256`, per-version sha256 in the index); `play-anon` = Google Play's own servers through an anonymous session (PlayAnonFetcher; fetches, sha256 per file, splits installed as one session); `play` = the Google Play deep-link — Play publishes NO APK URL, so the deep-link IS the official Play path and the row carries a visible 'needs Play' badge. Read by SourceResolver through PhoneAppActions.sources; `order` is the only legal ranking and an app's `sources` must be a subsequence of it. A `play` source carries NOTHING but its kind: a URL on it would be a fake. An app absent from `apps` still resolves — to the Play deep-link alone — so every package the vault or an import names has a row. Fleet (Cloud) apps are NOT here: they install through the constellation manifest and the updater's release path, one downloader for the fleet. VENDOR FIELDS: `apk` = URL template ({version} from the feed, {asset} from `abis`); `abis` = ABI -> asset fragment, chosen by AbiUpdateTag over Build.SUPPORTED_ABIS; `feed` = official JSON version endpoint, `version_name`/`version_code`/`apk_key`/`sha256_key` = dot paths into it; `version_re` = one-group regex normalising the feed's version string; `sha256` = URL of a sidecar whose body is a bare hex or the sha256sum(1) form. A vendor source with no feed has no version probe: it re-fetches whatever the vendor serves today and the updater's downgrade guard decides. EVIDENCE 2026-09-25 from this container: every `feed`, `apk` and `sha256` below answered 200 with the declared shape; F-Droid's api answered 404 for telegram/bitwarden/firefox/brave/obsidian/signal/whatsapp, which is why they carry no `fdroid` source; download.mozilla.org's fennec-latest redirector serves Firefox 68 (2020) and is deliberately NOT declared. #627 KINDS ARE DECLARED, AND THE PAGE'S SOURCE TABS ARE THAT DECLARATION. `kinds` carries one entry per kind named in `order`, and Store ▸ Phone draws one tab per entry, in `order`, labelled from `label`. Adding a kind here yields a tab with no Kotlin change; a kind in `order` with no `kinds` entry (or the reverse) fails to parse. `fetches` is the honest half: true = this store hands us bytes we can verify and version-compare ourselves (vendor, fdroid); false = it is a HAND-OFF, the row deep-links into that store's own page and there is no automated version compare, which the row says rather than implying one. `installer` is the store app the hand-off is aimed at, looked up in the top-level `sources` map — never named in code. `catalogue` says this kind is a different CLIENT for another kind's catalogue, not a catalogue of its own: Aurora Store serves Google Play's index, so `aurora` aliases `play` and its tab is every app with a `play` rung. Samsung's Galaxy Store is a genuinely separate catalogue, so `samsung` aliases nothing and its tab is exactly the apps that declare it.

vendor.label: Direct
vendor._doc: The publisher's OWN endpoint. This is the ticket's 'Direct' tab: the vendor rung IS installing straight from the people who built the app, so a separate Direct tab would have exactly the same membership as this one. One kind, one tab, labelled for what the user is choosing.

play-anon.label: Play (anonymous)
play-anon._doc: Google Play's OWN servers, reached the way Aurora Store reaches them, by this store alone: no Google account, no Play app, no Aurora app on the phone. An anonymous Play session is fetched from the first declared dispenser in `play_anon.dispensers` that answers (POST of the declared gplayapi device profile; the dispenser hands back an anonymous account's auth token + gsfId + device tokens), then details -> purchase (free offer) -> delivery give the base APK and every split APK on Google's CDN, each with a sha256 that every downloaded file must match before it goes near an installer (PlayAnonFetcher.kt). HONESTY RULE: a dispenser outage is reported as "Play token unavailable", never as "not installable" — the app is installable, the anonymous session is what is missing. `catalogue: play` because it IS Google Play's catalogue, through a client that is us.

samsung.label: Samsung
samsung._doc: Galaxy Store: a real, separate catalogue, and one with NO public APK endpoint and no public version API — its store API is device-authenticated and app-internal. So this rung is a hand-off: the row deep-links into the Galaxy Store page and says plainly that there is no automated version compare for it. Declaring it as a fetching source would be a claim about bytes we cannot get.

aurora.label: Aurora
aurora._doc: Aurora Store is a CLIENT for Google Play's catalogue, not an index of its own — so 'install via Aurora' is a different route to the SAME app set, and `catalogue: play` says exactly that. Its tab is therefore every app with a `play` rung, derived, rather than a per-app duplicate of the Play ladder. Aurora can install what Play can; it is not another catalogue and this file does not pretend it is.

play_anon._doc: Declared config of the play-anon rung. `dispensers` are tried IN ORDER; the first is Aurora Store's public dispenser (AuroraOSS/AuroraStore Constants.URL_DISPENSER), which answers only Aurora's own client User-Agent, so `user_agent` is declared with it rather than hidden in code. `device_profile` is an asset file copied byte-for-byte from AuroraOSS/gplayapi (pin: ab_cloud-libs-shared/libs/gplayapi/data/gplayapi-pin.json, GPL-3.0-or-later). `api` is Google Play's fdfe base. `token_ttl_minutes` bounds how long one anonymous session is reused before a fresh one is asked for; a 401 from Play also forces one fresh session. No dispenser URL is a Kotlin literal (ac_cloud-store/test/test-store-upstream-sources.sh).
